messages:
incident-bot: HIGH: Customer `penumbra` is receiving elevated 429s from dedicated pool `penumbra-prod-pool` (source: api-gateway). 2,100 429s/min over last 3m. Pager -> @oncall-ryd. Dashboard: https://internal.redwood/incs/1834567890

alice.m: seeing same in logs. spikes started ~1834567500. Impact: penumbra dashboards failing, some internal jobs retrying. tagging SRE/infra.

ben_ops: pinged infra team. quick question — is this a legitimate traffic surge or runaway CI? any repeatable UA or key?

claire_se: customer support (penumbra) says they kicked off a nightly sync earlier that should be low QPS. they confirm job retry loop possibly due to 503 -> retry.

dev_rel_june: customer asked for minimal disruption — they rely on dashboarding for live ops. can we do a temporary exempt for the dashboarding service account while we investigate?

alice.m: preliminary isolation: most 429s are from API key `penumbra-dashboard-key` and user_agent contains `penumbra-sync/1.2`. Suggest emergency rate-exemption for that key scoped to read-only endpoints.

oncall-ryd: i’m on it. quick mitigation options: 1) add temporary contract override (bypass 429 throttling) for that key for 2h; 2) route traffic to lower-cost fallback model (increase capacity) — option 1 is fastest.

ben_ops: +1 for override. we should scope it: restrict to GET endpoints and to model family `gptx-4-mini` and set token cap. also add audit metadata.

claire_se: also ensure customer is notified and billing/finance looped — overrides are billable. looping @finance-liaison.

alice.m: executing runbook step: create override via admin API. payload below (will redact token after run):

```bash
curl -X POST https://admin-api.internal.redwood/v1/overrides \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "customer_id":"penumbra",
    "key_id":"penumbra-dashboard-key",
    "scope": ["/v1/generate:read","/v1/embeddings:read"],
    "models": ["gptx-4-mini"],
    "token_cap": 100000,
    "expires_at": 1834568990,
    "reason": "temporary dashboard read exemption to mitigate 429s due to retry storm",
    "requester": "alice.m"
  }'
```

infra-bot: override request received (request_id=rq_83721). validating permissions...

oncall-ryd: running now. grant minimal scope and expire in 18m? Alice suggested 2h — go with 2h (consistent).

infra-bot: override applied (override_id=ov_2026pen). scope: read-only, models: gptx-4-mini, token_cap=100000, expires_at=1834568990. Audit: alice.m.

dev_rel_june: pinging penumbra-support: "we've applied a temporary read-only exemption for your dashboard key for 2 hours while we investigate. this is billable and will be reverted automatically."

penumbra-support: thanks, appreciate the fast response. we'll pause the nightly sync on our side too. do you want us to run any specific tests?

alice.m: please pause sync and run a single low-rate query to confirm dashboard connectivity. also collect request_id from next failing request if any.

ben_ops: monitoring: 429 rate dropped to ~30/min within 90s of exemption. overall error rate for customer down 94%. good signal.

claire_se: finance-liaison: FYI override applied. please open billing ticket and flag as emergency override charge.

finance-liaison: acknowledged. creating ticket FIN-7642, linking override ov_2026pen, tagging for expedited review.

alice.m: next steps: 1) await customer pause and logs; 2) hunt for root cause — look at retries in their sync and our gateway 5xx -> 429 cascade; 3) prepare rollback plan if override causes abuse. assigning postmortem to me.

oncall-ryd: will keep monitoring for next 30m and escalate to infra if we see anomalous token usage approaching cap. set alert: override_key_usage>80%.

infra-bot: alert created (ALERT-pen-override-usage). will notify if token usage > 80k.

ben_ops: found repeated 503s from backend service `penum-sync` between 1834567400-1834567600 leading to client retry amplification. tagging app-team.

alice.m: if backend 503s confirmed, root cause likely customer-side retries. mitigation = have customer add jitter/backoff. we'll keep override short.

penumbra-support: confirmed they saw spike from 1834567400, they will patch retries and redeploy within the hour.

claire_se: customer asked for confirmation that we won't change model or drop exemptions without notice. reassure them — it's auto-expire and we'll notify 5m before revoke.

dev_rel_june: noted. i’ll draft note for customer.

noncall-ryd: update 15m: token usage at 12k/100k, 429s < 5/min. continue monitoring.

alice.m: good. creating a short runbook note and will capture timeline for postmortem.

infra-bot: override ov_2026pen will auto-expire at 1834568990. reminder scheduled 5m prior.

ben_ops: also added temporary ACL rule to drop traffic from UA `penumbra-sync/1.2` to write endpoints — double protection.

claire_se: can we close this thread once override expires and no further 429s?

alice.m: yes — i'll update postmortem and close. postmortem owner: alice.m, timeline owner: ben_ops, customer comms: dev_rel_june.

penumbra-support: thanks team. super smooth.

infra-bot: override expired (override_id=ov_2026pen) at 1834568990. no further elevated 429s observed in 10m after expiry.

alice.m: closing incident. will file postmortem with remediation: add recommendations to allow short lived dashboard exemptions in contract, require request template, and surface client-side retry guidance.

dev_rel_june: will send formal wrap-up to customer and include next steps. :white_check_mark:

ben_ops: closing monitoring alerts and handoff to normal ops.

claire_se: marking incident resolved from customer ops side.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: penumbra elevated 429s — resolved via temporary contract override and customer retries fix. incident duration ~25m.
